input.quote: 14.6 Insurance. Each Party shall procure and maintain insurance, including product liability insurance, with respect to its activities hereunder and under the Ancillary Agreements and which is consistent with normal business practices of companies similarly situated
input.rationale: Clause 14.6 is the only insurance provision in the Agreement. It obliges each Party (including RevMed) to carry insurance, including product liability, but sets no monetary limits and no E&O or cyber/privacy coverage; "consistent with normal business practices" is not a quantified floor. It therefore fails the fallback, which requires professional errors and omissions coverage of at least USD 1,000,000 and cyber and privacy coverage of at least USD 2,000,000. We proposed the shortest fix: a new 14.7 imposing those two fallback minimums on RevMed, leaving 14.6's evidence-on-request, notice and self-insurance mechanics intact (14.6's evidence-upon-request sentence already covers certificates, but that is a preferred-level element and is not relied on here).

ops.text: Insurance Minimums. RevMed shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 and cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Clause 14.6 sets no minimum limits, so we added the two coverages our playbook requires at the fallback level: E&O of USD 1,000,000 and cyber liability of USD 2,000,000 for RevMed. The existing evidence-on-request and self-insurance mechanics are untouched.
proposal.summary: Add RevMed E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M minimum insurance limits.

mappings.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
